svg.title: Big-O is a shape, not a speed
svg.desc: A whiteboard sketch with four labelled growth curves for constant, logarithmic, linear and quadratic work; two lines of identical linear complexity measured a million elements apart, one an array walk at 32.6 milliseconds and one a shuffled linked-list walk at 661 milliseconds with a 20.3 times gap arrowed between them; a crossover plot where an n-squared curve sits below an n-log-n curve until about forty elements, with the advice to always pick the lower Big-O crossed out in red; and nine groups of three tally marks illustrating the accounting argument that makes a doubling array's append amortized constant time.
svg.text: Big-O is a shape, not a speed
Big-O is the SHAPE of the curve
same Big-O. 20x apart, because one of them chases pointers.
Big-O throws the constant away. Your laptop
does not. At n = 1000 all three fit in L2
below this the "worse" algorithm is faster:
every real sort switches to insertion sort on small runs
when the array doubles, the banked tokens pay for the copy.
so append is O(1) amortized - never O(1) worst case.
